identity: The complete Surat al-Nahl (Quran 16), all 128 ayat, in Uthmani orthography with the diacritics and verse markers stripped (al-malaikah spelled al-malikah, al-samawat spelled al-samut, ayah spelled ayah without alif). 1844 tokens, ZERO <NL>: the whole sura is one printed block.
law: SCRIPTURE - THE VERSE IS THE UNIT (doctrine 0k). For the Quran this is stronger than for the Gospel of Luke, because the ayah marker IS the deleted punctuation: every gold boundary is an end-of-ayah and nothing else. Inside an ayah NOTHING cuts - not fa of consequence, not an imperative, not parallel clauses, not wa + a new finite predication, not a question. 1844 tokens / 128 ayat = 14.4 tokens per unit, the same arithmetic that identified the Luke passage in 0k.
reasoning: The decisive check was arithmetic before syntax: 1844 tokens with no line structure at all, and a text I can identify verse by verse, gives 14.4 tokens per unit with min 4 (v.117 mata qalil wa-lahum adhab alim) and max 32 (v.61) - exactly the profile of a verse-segmented scripture and nothing like the 8-token over-cutting I fall into when I let PASS-2 laws fire. So I refused every internal candidate. Cases where my old rules would have fired and are wrong here: v.1 fa-la tastajiluhu (fa of prohibition inside the verse); v.4 fa-idha huwa khasim mubin (A8 says fa-idha always cuts - not in scripture); v.22 fa-lladhina la yuminuna (fa of consequence); v.29 fa-dkhulu abwaba jahannam (imperative, E6 - already killed by 0k); v.30 the question wa-qila li-lladhina ittaqaw madha anzala rabbukum qalu khayran plus its answer plus two further wa-clauses, ALL one ayah; v.36 fa-siru fi al-ard fa-nzuru (two chained imperatives, one ayah); v.75 hal yastawuna al-hamdu li-llah bal aktharuhum la yalamun (a question, a pious formula and a bal-correction inside ONE ayah - three separate triggers in my table, all suppressed); v.125 udu ila sabili rabbik ... wa-jadilhum ... inna rabbaka (imperative + wa-imperative + inna-clause, one ayah); v.127 wa-sbir ... wa-la tahzan ... wa-la taku (three imperatives, one ayah). The two places where I had to think were the twin ayat that end in the same word - v.30/31 both end al-muttaqin and v.96/97 both end yamalun - and the internal repetition in v.20 (la yakhluquna shayan wa-hum yukhlaqun, both spelled yakhluqun), where the boundary is the SECOND occurrence, not the first. All 128 ends were located in order and the last one lands exactly on the final token of the document, which is the strongest possible confirmation that the alignment did not drift.
